performanceGate.scope: Controlled API-only authenticated HTTP upload completion, not media-ready throughput or whole application
performanceGate.method: Each deployment round is one paired block; log ratio of its 20-upload medians. Resample whole paired blocks 10000 times, seed 0. Positive means candidate slower. No individual-request independence assumption.
performanceGate.limitations: Six paired blocks on one host give limited precision; bootstrap interval is exploratory, not a formal release qualification. The 5% budget was chosen before this controlled run completed. Default-background-work smoke remains inconclusive regardless of this result.

workload.fixture: 512x512 RGB seeded random PNG, different bytes each round/index, identical between versions
workload.preflight: 1000 entries, alternating existing/new, mixed hex/base64; 3 warmups and 12 measured requests per round

limitations: Loopback HTTP on one shared 2-core host. Sequential requests only; microservices workers excluded in this controlled run. ML disabled. Fresh per-version volumes at start, then retained between rounds. No WAN/TLS/mobile testing. Upload HTTP completion does not mean all background jobs completed. Existing candidate production dependency/native-codec image reused with freshly built full server dist; web/CLI remain from prior build. Sample counts are specified under workload; sequential small-file measurements are not a capacity test.
controlledLimitations: Controlled mode disables microservices workers equally for both builds, leaving real authenticated HTTP, checksum/deduplication, PostgreSQL durability and storage writes enabled. Queued media/geodata work does not execute. This isolates upload request completion and does not measure media-ready throughput.
